actions.action: Require a supplied source passage for every definition.
actions.mechanism: Enforce source linkage at the storage boundary.
actions.implementation: Create a supplied-passages registry. Require each definition’s source_passage_id to reference an existing registry entry. Reject missing or unknown IDs on every write path; provide no external-source lookup.
actions.check: Attempt to save definitions with absent, unknown, and valid passage IDs. Only the valid reference succeeds.
actions.risk: A valid reference proves linkage, not that the passage supports the wording.

actions.action: Store competing definitions without overwriting either wording.
actions.mechanism: Represent each wording as a separate definition attached to the same term.
actions.implementation: Give each alternative its own definition ID, exact wording, and required source passage ID. Make “Add competing wording” distinct from “Edit.” Preserve prior wording when edits occur.
actions.check: Add two conflicting definitions and edit one. Both alternatives and the edited definition’s previous wording remain inspectable with their source IDs.
actions.risk: Minor variants may accumulate; grouping must not silently merge their wording.

actions.action: Make each definition’s source directly inspectable.
actions.mechanism: Place source evidence beside the wording it supports.
actions.implementation: Add a “View passage” control to every definition. Open the complete supplied passage with its ID in an adjacent panel. If highlighting a supporting span, retain the unhighlighted surrounding passage.
actions.check: From each displayed alternative, open its exact stored passage without leaving the term. Verify the displayed text matches the stored passage.
actions.risk: A selected highlight can bias interpretation; readers must still see the complete passage.

actions.action: Record what is disputed, not just a disputed badge.
actions.mechanism: Attach explicit disagreement records to definition IDs.
actions.implementation: Provide a dispute form containing the challenged definition, objection, competing wording if present, and relevant supplied passage IDs. Store competing wording as a source-linked definition. Keep resolved objections visible with their resolution rationale.
actions.check: Create and resolve a dispute. A reader can still inspect the original objection, competing wording, source passages, and resolution.
actions.risk: Resolution may be mistaken for consensus; label it as an editorial decision.

actions.action: Prevent source corrections from silently changing a definition’s evidence.
actions.mechanism: Keep passage versions immutable and flag affected definitions.
actions.implementation: Treat a corrected passage as a new passage ID linked to its predecessor. Retain the old passage, flag definitions referencing it for review, and require an explicit relinking decision. Block deletion of referenced passages.
actions.check: Correct a passage used by two definitions. Both retain their original evidence and receive review flags; neither changes its reference automatically.
actions.risk: Review work can accumulate, so pending flags must remain visible.

actions.action: Separate different senses from competing wording.
actions.mechanism: Distinguish disagreement about one meaning from definitions describing different meanings.
actions.implementation: Allow an editor to group source-linked definitions into labeled senses. Require an explicit choice between “another sense” and “competing wording,” while permitting later reclassification without deleting definitions or disputes.
actions.check: Create two senses and a dispute within one. Readers can distinguish the senses and identify precisely which alternatives compete.
actions.risk: Sense splitting could conceal disagreement; preserve reclassification history and existing dispute links.

actions.action: Expose disagreement before readers open a term.
actions.mechanism: Carry disagreement status into glossary navigation.
actions.implementation: Show alternative counts and unresolved-dispute labels in term lists and search results. Add a disputed-terms filter. On term pages, show all alternatives without collapsing nonpreferred wording by default.
actions.check: For a term with two alternatives and an unresolved dispute, verify that lists, search results, the filter, and the term page expose that state.
actions.risk: Unlabeled counts may imply that every alternative is disputed; distinguish alternatives from active disputes.
